title: Chicken Caesar Salad Wraps
ingredients: 1 cup grilled chicken breast (sliced; use tofu for a vegetarian/vegan option)
¼ cup grated Parmesan cheese (dairy‑free Parmesan for dairy-free/vegan version)
¼ cup Caesar dressing (or vegan Caesar dressing)
substitutions: Use a dairy‑free cheese and gluten‑free wraps if needed.
instructions: In a large bowl, toss chopped romaine with chicken, Parmesan, and Caesar dressing.
Lay out tortillas and divide the salad evenly.
Add croutons if desired and roll up each tortilla tightly.
Wrap in foil or store in airtight containers for easy meal prep.
mealPreppingTip: Prepare the salad a few hours ahead and assemble the wraps just before serving to keep the tortillas from getting soggy.

title: Quinoa & Black Bean Salad with Avocado
ingredients: 1 cup black beans, rinsed and drained
1 ripe avocado, cubed (add just before serving for freshness)
substitutions: Use extra lime juice instead of cilantro if you prefer.
instructions: In a large bowl, combine quinoa, black beans, bell pepper, and tomatoes.
In a separate small bowl, whisk together lime juice, olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Pour the dressing over the salad and toss to coat.
Gently fold in the avocado cubes and cilantro right before serving.
mealPreppingTip: Store the base salad in an airtight container and add the avocado and cilantro fresh when ready to enjoy.

title: Mediterranean Chickpea Bowl
ingredients: ¼ cup Kalamata olives, pitted and sliced
¼ cup crumbled feta cheese (or dairy‑free alternative for vegan)
2 cups mixed greens (spinach, arugula, or lettuce)
Salt, pepper, and 1 tsp dried oregano
substitutions: Omit or replace with a dairy‑free cheese for a vegan version.
instructions: In a bowl, combine chickpeas, cherry tomatoes, cucumber, olives, and mixed greens.
Sprinkle the feta cheese over the top.
In a small jar, combine olive oil, lemon juice, oregano, salt, and pepper; shake well.
Drizzle the dressing over the bowl just before eating.
mealPreppingTip: Pack ingredients separately in meal prep containers and combine when ready to serve for maximum freshness.

title: Turkey & Avocado Club Sandwich
ingredients: 2 slices whole grain or gluten‑free bread
3–4 slices lean turkey breast (or smoked tofu for vegetarian/vegan options)
1 tsp Dijon mustard or vegan mustard
substitutions: Use gluten‑free bread and check labels for additives if needed.
instructions: Toast the bread slices lightly if desired.
Spread mustard on one side of each slice.
Layer turkey (or tofu), avocado, tomato, and lettuce on one slice.
Season with salt and pepper before topping with the second slice.
Cut diagonally and serve.
mealPreppingTip: For meal prep, pack the components separately and assemble the sandwich just before eating to maintain texture.

title: Grilled Vegetable & Hummus Wrap
ingredients: 1 large whole wheat or gluten‑free tortilla
½ cup hummus (choose your favorite flavor)
Salt, pepper, and dried herbs (oregano or basil)
allergenWarning: Contains gluten and sesame in hummus
substitutions: Use gluten‑free tortillas and substitute hummus with a bean spread if sesame is a concern.
instructions: Preheat grill or grill pan to medium-high heat.
Toss zucchini, bell pepper, and eggplant slices with olive oil, salt, pepper, and herbs.
Grill the vegetables for 3–4 minutes per side until tender and slightly charred.
Spread hummus evenly over the tortilla; layer the grilled vegetables on top.
Roll tightly and slice in half to serve.
mealPreppingTip: Grill extra vegetables and store them in an airtight container. Assemble the wrap fresh for the best texture.

title: Asian-Inspired Lettuce Wraps
ingredients: 1 lb ground chicken, turkey, or plant-based crumbles
2 tbsp soy sauce (or tamari for gluten‑free)
1 tbsp hoisin sauce (optional; check for allergens)
1 head butter or iceberg lettuce (leaves separated)
Chopped green onions and sesame seeds for garnish
substitutions: Use tamari for gluten-free and a gluten‑free hoisin sauce if needed.
instructions: In a large pan, heat sesame oil over medium heat. Add onion, garlic, and ginger; sauté until fragrant.
Add ground chicken (or alternative) and cook until no longer pink, about 5–7 minutes.
Stir in soy sauce, hoisin sauce, and chili paste.
Add carrots and bell pepper; cook for another 2–3 minutes until slightly tender.
Spoon the filling into separated lettuce leaves.
Garnish with green onions and sesame seeds.
mealPreppingTip: Store the cooked filling and lettuce leaves separately. Reheat the filling, then serve in fresh lettuce wraps at mealtime.

title: Pesto Pasta Salad with Veggies
ingredients: 8 oz whole grain or gluten‑free pasta
½ cup pesto (basil or sun‑dried tomato; use dairy‑free pesto for a vegan version)
allergenWarning: Contains gluten in standard pasta and potential dairy in pesto.
substitutions: Use gluten‑free pasta and vegan pesto if needed.
instructions: Cook the pasta according to package instructions; drain and rinse under cold water.
In a large bowl, combine pasta, cherry tomatoes, spinach, and zucchini slices.
Add pesto and olive oil; toss until evenly coated.
Season with salt and pepper.
mealPreppingTip: Store in an airtight container. Taste may improve the next day as flavors meld, or add a splash of olive oil before serving.

title: Vietnamese Rice Paper Rolls
ingredients: 1 cup shredded lettuce or mixed greens
1 cup cooked shrimp, chicken, or tofu strips
For the dipping sauce: ¼ cup hoisin sauce mixed with 1 tbsp peanut butter and a splash of water
substitutions: Use a peanut-free sauce or sunflower seed butter if peanut allergies are a concern.
instructions: Soak each rice paper in warm water for about 20–30 seconds until soft, then lay on a flat surface.
Place a small amount of lettuce, shrimp (or chicken/tofu), carrots, bean sprouts, cucumber, and herbs in the center of the wrapper.
Fold in the sides and roll tightly like a burrito.
Repeat with remaining ingredients.
Serve with the peanut hoisin dipping sauce.
mealPreppingTip: Prepare and store components separately. Soak and roll the papers fresh at mealtime for the best texture.

title:
Caprese Chicken 
 Salad
ingredients: 2 cups mixed greens (arugula, spinach, or baby kale)
substitutions: Use dairy‑free mozzarella for a dairy-free version.
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the mixed greens, cherry tomatoes, and mozzarella.
Add sliced grilled chicken and tear fresh basil leaves on top.
Drizzle with olive oil and balsamic glaze.
Season with salt and pepper, then toss gently.
mealPreppingTip: Pack ingredients in separate containers and combine when ready to serve to avoid wilting.

title: Falafel Bowl with Tahini Sauce
ingredients: 1 batch baked or cooked falafel (store‑bought or homemade)
2 cups mixed greens or baby spinach
½ cup cooked quinoa or couscous
For the dressing: 3 tbsp tahini, juice of 1 lemon, 1 garlic clove (minced), water to thin, salt to taste
allergenWarning: Contains sesame in tahini and gluten if couscous is used.
substitutions: Use gluten‑free grains (like quinoa) and a tahini alternative if sesame is an issue.
instructions: Arrange mixed greens, quinoa, tomatoes, cucumber, and red onion in a bowl.
Add falafel on top.
In a small bowl, whisk together tahini, lemon juice, minced garlic, and enough water to create a smooth, drizzle‑able consistency; season with salt.
Drizzle the sauce over the bowl and serve.
mealPreppingTip: Falafel can be made in large batches and stored in airtight containers. Pack the vegetables and dressing separately to assemble fresh.

title: Sweet Potato & Black Bean Tacos
ingredients: 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
1 can black beans, rinsed and drained
instructions: Toss sweet potato cubes in olive oil, chili powder, cumin, salt, and pepper. Roast in a 400°F (200°C) oven for 25–30 minutes until tender and lightly caramelized.
In a bowl, combine roasted sweet potatoes and black beans.
Warm tortillas and fill with the sweet potato–black bean mixture.
Top with avocado slices, a sprinkle of cilantro, and a squeeze of lime.
mealPreppingTip: Pre-roast a large batch of sweet potatoes and store them with the beans in airtight containers. Reheat and assemble tacos when ready.

title: Buddha Bowl with Roasted Veggies & Tahini Dressing
ingredients: 1 cup cooked brown rice or quinoa
1 cup roasted chickpeas (seasoned with paprika and garlic powder)
1 cup mixed raw or steamed veggies (carrots, spinach, red cabbage)
For the dressing: 3 tbsp tahini, juice of 1 lemon, 1 tbsp maple syrup, water to thin, salt to taste
substitutions: Use a sunflower seed butter-based dressing if sesame allergies are a concern.
instructions: In a bowl, layer the cooked rice/quinoa, roasted veggies, chickpeas, and fresh vegetables.
Whisk together tahini, lemon juice, maple syrup, and enough water in a small bowl to achieve your desired consistency; season with salt.
Drizzle the dressing over the bowl before serving.
mealPreppingTip: Assemble individual bowls in advance. Keep the dressing separately and add right before eating for optimal texture.

title:
Lentil & Vegetable 
 Soup
ingredients: 4 cups vegetable broth (check for gluten if sensitive)
1 tsp dried thyme and 1 tsp cumin
substitutions: Use a homemade vegetable broth to control ingredients.
instructions: In a large pot, heat olive oil over medium heat; sauté onion, garlic, carrots, and celery until soft, about 5–7 minutes.
Stir in lentils, diced tomatoes, vegetable broth, thyme, and cumin.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and let simmer for 25–30 minutes, until lentils are tender.
Season with salt and pepper before serving.
mealPreppingTip: Soups taste better the next day; store in portioned containers and reheat as needed.

title: Mason Jar Salad with Layered Protein
ingredients: ½ cup protein (grilled chicken, tofu, or beans)
Optional: ¼ cup crumbled feta or dairy‑free cheese
substitutions: Use a dairy‑free cheese and ensure your dressing is allergen‑friendly.
instructions: In a mason jar, add the dressing to the bottom.
Layer harder vegetables first (carrots, cucumbers, bell pepper) followed by tomatoes and greens.
Top with your protein and cheese.
When ready to eat, shake the jar to distribute the dressing or transfer to a bowl.
mealPreppingTip: Mason jar salads can be assembled a few days ahead; keeping the dressing separate helps prevent sogginess.

title:
Tofu Stir‑Fry Rice 
 Bowl
ingredients: 1 block firm tofu, pressed and cubed (use tempeh for variation)
2 cups mixed stir‑fry vegetables (broccoli, bell peppers, snap peas)
2 cups cooked brown rice or cauliflower rice
2 tbsp soy sauce (or tamari for gluten‑free)
Optional: red pepper flakes for heat
substitutions: Use tamari for a gluten‑free option.
instructions: In a non‑stick pan, heat sesame oil over medium-high heat.
Add tofu cubes and cook until lightly golden on all sides, about 5–7 minutes. Remove tofu from the pan.
In the same pan, add garlic, ginger, and mixed vegetables; sauté until vegetables are crisp‑tender (about 3–4 minutes).
Return tofu to the pan and drizzle with soy sauce; toss to coat evenly.
Serve the stir‑fry over warm rice.
mealPreppingTip: Prepare and store the tofu and veggies separately from the rice; reheat together before serving for a fresher taste.

title:
Cold Soba Noodle 
 Salad
ingredients: 8 oz soba noodles (choose 100% buckwheat for gluten‑free or substitute with rice noodles)
For the dressing: 3 tbsp soy sauce (or tamari), 1 tbsp rice vinegar, 1 tsp sesame oil, 1 tsp honey or maple syrup, 1 garlic clove (minced)
substitutions: Use rice noodles for a gluten‑free version and adjust sauce for sesame allergies.
instructions: Cook soba noodles or your chosen alternative according to package instructions; rinse under cold water and drain well.
In a large bowl, combine the noodles, carrots, bell pepper, edamame, and green onions.
Whisk together the dressing ingredients in a small bowl and pour over the salad.
Toss well to coat and serve chilled.
mealPreppingTip: Store the cold noodle salad in airtight containers in the refrigerator. It can be enjoyed as a light lunch or side dish.

title: Zucchini Noodle & Tomato Salad
ingredients: ¼ cup basil pesto (or dairy‑free pesto)
substitutions: Use a dairy‑free pesto or homemade basil blend without cheese.
instructions: Place zucchini noodles in a large bowl.
Add cherry tomatoes and red onion slices.
Drizzle with olive oil and toss with pesto until well coated.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
mealPreppingTip: Zucchini noodles are best prepared fresh. You can store the pesto separately and toss together right before serving.

title: Stuffed Bell Peppers with Ground Turkey & Veggies
ingredients: 4 bell peppers (any color), tops cut off and seeds removed
1 lb ground turkey (or plant-based crumbles for a vegetarian option)
½ cup shredded cheese (optional; use dairy‑free cheese for dairy-free)
substitutions: Use a vegan ground alternative and dairy‑free cheese for a plant‑based version.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a skillet, heat olive oil over medium heat. Sauté diced onion and garlic until softened, about 3–4 minutes.
Add ground turkey (or alternative) and cook until browned; stir in diced tomatoes, Italian seasoning, salt, and pepper.
Stir in the cooked rice and remove from heat.
Stuff each bell pepper with the turkey‑rice mixture and place in a baking dish. Top with shredded cheese if using.
Cover with foil and bake for 30 minutes; remove the foil and bake an additional 10 minutes until the peppers are tender and cheese is melted.
mealPreppingTip: Prepare stuffed peppers in advance and reheat in the oven or microwave when ready to serve.
